prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: hit while turning left in Conroe, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported concussion. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1410; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage does not match the story: the dents are on another side and at another height than the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Officers responded to a two-vehicle collision in Conroe, Texas, in which Driver 1 was turning left when Driver 2's vehicle struck it. Driver 1 reported a concussion and complained of headache and dizziness at the scene. The injury is consistent with the type and force of a collision of this kind.

Driver 2 confirmed that the collision happened as Driver 1 described. Two witnesses gave statements that matched this account, and scene photographs show both vehicles resting in the positions described. Officers also confirmed that Driver 1 was in the vehicle at the time, and a Passenger seated in the rear was identified and likewise confirmed to be present.

On inspection, however, the damage to Driver 1's vehicle does not match the account. The dents and deformation are on a different side of the vehicle and at a different height than the area that would have been struck in the described impact. No earlier damage to the vehicle is known to officers or to the witnesses.

Driver 1 is the named driver on the policy covering the vehicle.
